saints.name: St. Francis Borgia
saints.title: Priest
saints.shortBlurb: A Spanish duke who, shaken by the sight of a dead empress's ruined beauty, left his rank to become a Jesuit…
biography: Born at Gandía in Valencia on 28 October 1510, great-grandson of Pope Alexander VI and of King Ferdinand of Aragon, Francis married Eleanor de Castro in 1529 and rose at the court of Charles V to be Viceroy of Catalonia and fourth Duke of Gandía. In 1539 he convoyed the corpse of the Empress Isabella to Granada, and the sight of her ruined beauty turned his heart from the world.

Widowed in 1546, he entered the Society of Jesus and was ordained priest in 1551, as commissary-general in Spain founding a dozen colleges. Elected the order's third Superior General in 1565, he governed its rapid spread through Europe and the missions of the New World so fruitfully that he has been called its second founder. He died in Rome on 30 September 1572.

Beatified in 1624 and canonized by Clement X, he has been invoked against earthquakes since the time of his beatification, a patronage spread through Jesuit churches, and Portugal claimed him as a patron of the kingdom. His feast was long kept on 10 October.
saints.knownFor: Renouncing a dukedom to serve as a Jesuit.
